prompt: A baby's weight is heavier than 80 of every 100 babies the same age.
why: Heavier than 80 of every 100 babies of the same age means 80% are below. That rank is the 80th percentile.
trap: It's a rank, not an average.

prompt: A test result says you scored better than 95% of test takers.
why: Scoring better than 95% of test takers puts you at the 95th percentile. Percentiles rank a value against everyone else.
trap: It ranks you, it doesn't average.

prompt: A website promises that 99% of pages load in under 2 seconds.
tells: 99% of pages load in under 2 seconds
why: 99% of pages loading under 2 seconds means 2 seconds is the 99th percentile. Targets like this describe the slow tail, not the average.
trap: An average could hide slow pages; this doesn't.

prompt: Scholarships go to applicants in the top 10%.
why: The top 10% is everyone above the 90th percentile. Cutoffs by rank are percentiles.

prompt: A running app ranks your 5K time against others your age and says you beat 70%.
why: Beating 70% of runners your age means 70% are below you. That's the 70th percentile.

prompt: Salary data is shown as the values 25%, 50% and 75% of the way up the sorted list.
why: Values 25%, 50% and 75% of the way up the sorted list are percentiles, also called quartiles. The 50% mark is the median.
trap: The 50% one is the median, but the set is percentiles.
